audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven chart rows disagreed with the packet chart and with the mirror: Level 1 read Gnar, Level 2 'Skill', Levels 3 and 4-5 Renekton, and both item rows Renekton — while whys[3], whys[5] and whys[6] on the same page describe Gnar owning every one of those windows.
audit.why: 49.56% over 1947 games. Packet chart is Renekton, Gnar, Skill, Gnar, Gnar, Gnar, Gnar and the mirror (gnar__renekton) flipped all six rows to that shape as one atomic group.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-3, 5 and 6 flipped in matched full/content pairs; ratings set inverse to the mirror's (L1 6/10, Gnar rows 3-4/10, L3 5/10).

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item row credited your Eclipse, but spikes[2] on the same page says Gnar's Heartsteel/Kraken spike is what changes that window. The 2+-item row claimed your side-lane pattern is at full power against a champion the page itself says kites your whole kit.
audit.why: Gnar out-ranges you at 1100 on Q and resets Hop on takedowns; his item spike lands into your Eclipse window.
audit.corrected: phases[5].why and phases[6].why rewritten to the real spike story; phases[3].why now keys to the Rage bar.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page treated 'GNAR!' as a generic Mega all-in and never stated the two interactions that decide fights: GNAR! only stuns if you are thrown into a wall (otherwise it is damage and a slow), and Mega's W is a separate area stun (Wallop) on a 7s cooldown. Hop's 22s rank-1 cooldown — your actual punish window — was never given.
audit.why: Gnar R: 'Any enemy that hits a wall is stunned and takes bonus damage.' Gnar W in Mega form: 'smash down on the area in front of him, stunning enemies', 7s. Gnar E: 22/19.5/17/14.5/12.
audit.corrected: Wall condition and Wallop stated in report[5].t; Hop's cooldown made the commit trigger in dosFull[0].d; Mega's stun and bulk stated in dontsFull[1].d; the Q return-pass slow stated in dosFull[2].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Only engage once it is down or baited' pointed at the ultimate rather than the cooldown you can actually punish.
audit.why: Gnar's escape is Hop at 22s rank 1; his R at rank 1 is 90s but is only decisive near terrain.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d now keys the commit to a spent Hop.

audit.why: The packet flagged 'Bait Boomerang Throw' and 'Spam Boomerang Throw' as probable wrong names; the kit confirms Boomerang Throw is Gnar's real mini-form Q. Both are false positives from the leading verb.

edits.before: Fury autos bully the first waves. Identify how Gnar contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Fury autos out-trade mini-Gnar in melee range — walk him off the wave between Boomerang Throw casts.

edits.before: Gnar has range at level 1 and you have no dash yet — his Boomerang Throw pokes safely while your Q cannot reach him, so he dictates the first wave.
edits.after: Boomerang Throw is his only level-1 tool and it is 16s down if he misses the catch — step onto him between throws, where Fury autos beat mini-Gnar's base damage.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around GNAR!'s cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: His Rage bar fills off every auto and Q — fight only on an empty bar, and never within a wall's length of terrain.

edits.before: Eclipse is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on GNAR!'s cooldown.
edits.after: His first item makes the poke real — your Eclipse window shuts before you can cash it.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Gnar carry threat 8/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Full-build Gnar kites the whole kit — 1100-range Q out-ranges your E and Hop resets on takedowns. Catch him in mini form.

edits.before: His Mega all-in. Avoid the transform. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Hop is his escape, 22s at rank 1 — commit when it is spent, not when Rage is full.

edits.before: Track Gnar's GNAR! (Mega Stun): His Mega all-in. Avoid the transform. When it is down — W-stun + Q him.
edits.after: GNAR! only stuns if you hit a wall — fight in open ground. Mega's Wallop is a separate area stun on 7s.

edits.before: Gnar wastes GNAR! (Mega Stun) — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: It slows on the return pass too — step out of its line, not just its throw.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Mega gets Wallop's stun and a bigger health bar — wait for Rage decay.

notes: Level 1 is the one row I am not fully comfortable with: the packet chart and the mirror both give it to Renekton, but the existing whys[0] argued the opposite from Gnar's 500-range mini form. I followed the mirror and rewrote the why to a defensible line (his Q is 16s at rank 1 if he does not catch it, and mini-Gnar's melee-range trade is weak), but the user may want the row re-checked. Mirror also noted report[8].t lists Sterak's Gage as core in a lane where the enemy has no shield to break — build call, left alone.
